en: A bill becomes a law when both the Senate and the House of Representatives approve the exact same text and the President signs it.
The President can stop a passed bill from becoming a law by using a veto, which Congress can only override with a two-thirds majority.
The Supreme Court can cancel a new law if a citizen challenges it and the justices rule that it violates the Constitution.
In early barangays, the datu acted as the chief executive and judge, but he had to consult the elders before declaring war or making major laws.
To join the secret Katipunan society, Andres Bonifacio required new members to sign a blood compact using their own blood to prove their absolute loyalty.
Jose Rizal wrote Noli Me Tangere and El Filibusterismo to expose Spanish colonial abuses, which awakened Filipino nationalism and inspired the revolution.
The Ifugao people irrigate their mountain rice terraces by channeling spring water from the forest canopy above through a system of bamboo pipes.
Dr. Fe del Mundo designed a bamboo incubator that uses a hot water bottle and an electric lightbulb to keep premature babies warm in rural areas.
Dancers perform the traditional Sinulog dance to mimic the flowing river current, honoring the Santo Niño during Cebu's annual festival.
The galleon trade connected the Philippines to Mexico by exchanging Chinese silk and porcelain for Mexican silver across the Pacific Ocean.
During national elections, registered Filipino voters shade the oval next to their chosen candidates on a ballot, which a machine then reads to count votes.
The traditional Bayanihan practice allows a community to relocate an entire nipa hut by having neighbors carry the structure on bamboo poles to a new site.
